Bone text overlays appear as narration advances: 'There is no backup.' at ~0:18, then fade. 'Most critical supply chain in the global economy.' at ~0:26. Subtle slow drift (Ken Burns: 1.03x scale over 23s) ensures no frozen state.
scenes.overlay_notes: Two bone text overlays: 'No backup.' and 'Most critical supply chain.' Timed to narration beats. Amber catchlight animation on wafer image is the primary motion element. No diagram yet.
scenes.shot_intent: Ground the abstract claim in a physical object — the wafer is the literal subject of the entire video. First visual payload.
scenes.information_role: The wafer is the object that everything depends on. The amber light on it signals it is the leverage point, before any diagram appears.

scenes.description: Supply chain flow diagram — 5 nodes build left to right as narration names each layer. GSAP sequential timeline: node appears (circle + label), then arrow draws to next node, then next node appears. Order: [EDA] → [Fabless Design] → [Foundry] → [OSAT] → [OEM]. All nodes: cyan (#3F8FA3) outline, bone label on near-black. IBM Plex Mono for node labels. Arrows: cyan, 2px. Sub-labels: IBM Plex Mono, muted steel, smaller. EDA sub-label: 'U.S.-dominated / 40%+ global share'. OSAT sub-label: 'Taiwan / S. Korea / SE Asia'. Nodes appear ~every 12–15s matching narration pace. On 'this is where the system narrows' — Foundry node border pulses and dims. Full diagram holds visible after all 5 nodes are placed.
scenes.overlay_notes: 5 sequential state changes (one per node reveal) + final pulse on Foundry node. Compliant with 4s rule — nodes appear ~every 12–15s, each node arrival is a clear state change. Sub-labels add visual density without cluttering the main flow.
scenes.shot_intent: Show the viewer the structure they did not know existed. Each node arrival is an information beat. The diagram is the argument.
scenes.information_role: The viewer learns the 5-layer supply chain structure: EDA → Fabless → Foundry → OSAT → OEM. Each layer is distinct. The Foundry layer is visually centered.

required_assets.description: GSAP supply chain diagram: 5-node sequential build. Cyan nodes + arrows on near-black. IBM Plex Mono labels. Sub-labels for EDA and OSAT concentration. Foundry node pulse at narration beat.

scenes.description: Chokepoint reveal — first hero moment. Supply chain diagram from sc08 persists. GSAP: (1) Foundry node border transitions from cyan to amber (#F5A400) over 0.8s, (2) all other nodes dim to 25% opacity over 0.6s, (3) a second amber ring pulses outward from the Foundry node and fades, (4) label beneath Foundry node updates: 'TSMC' — appears in amber, holds. Amber holds. Silence beat of 1.5s built into narration ('this is where the system narrows' — then pause). Full hold for remainder of sc09 with dim ambient glow animation on amber node.
scenes.overlay_notes: This is the first structural reveal. Amber = control/chokepoint in the Asymmetric color system. The Foundry node holds amber for the remainder of the video. Do not return it to cyan at any point.
scenes.shot_intent: The moment the supply chain collapses to one node. Everything before was structure — this is the leverage point being named.
scenes.information_role: The Foundry layer is the chokepoint. TSMC is identified. The color shift is the argument made visually.

required_assets.description: Continuation of sc08 diagram — GSAP: Foundry node cyan→amber transition, other nodes dim, second amber pulse ring, 'TSMC' label in amber appears

scenes.description: TSMC identity reveal — dossier-style. Near-black background. GSAP sequential text stagger: (1) 'TSMC' — large, amber, Space Grotesk Display, center-left, (2) 'Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Company' — smaller, bone, Inter Regular, (3) three data points appear as IBM Plex Mono lines staggered: 'Founded 1987 / Hsinchu, Taiwan' then '~60,000 employees' then 'Revenue: ~$125B (2025)'. Each line arrives 0.4s after previous. (4) On 'no other company on earth currently matches' — all text dims except 'TSMC', which holds amber. Amber node motif from sc09 is visible in the background at low opacity as a visual anchor.
scenes.overlay_notes: Dossier visual language. Data lines in IBM Plex Mono signal factual layer. Final state: TSMC name alone in amber — the rest of the information steps back. 4 distinct state changes across 48s.
scenes.shot_intent: Name the subject precisely before making the market-share claim. The viewer needs to understand what TSMC is and its scale before the 90%+ figure lands.
scenes.information_role: TSMC is the foundry. It is large, it is old (established, not new), and it is in one place. Revenue signals it is not a startup — it is a mature industrial institution.

required_assets.description: GSAP dossier stagger: TSMC name amber, full name bone, three IBM Plex Mono data lines, final dim-to-TSMC state

scenes.description: Supply chain diagram returns — same layout as sc08/sc09, Foundry node still amber. 90%+ stat card overlay fades in at 'industry analysts estimate TSMC's market share is above ninety percent': amber border, bone '$' removed — just '90%+' in large Inter, label below 'TSMC advanced-node market share (analyst est.)' in IBM Plex Mono, muted steel. Stat card holds 8s then fades to 30% opacity as narration continues. Samsung and Intel nodes are NOT shown in this diagram — supply chain shows only the foundry layer dominance. Background: near-black.
scenes.overlay_notes: Stat card must carry '(analyst est.)' qualifier per source_map c03 guidance. Hard stat card treatment permitted at medium-high confidence. No TSMC logo — wordmark only. Stat card fades to partial opacity rather than disappearing so it persists as a visual reference.
scenes.shot_intent: Quantify the dominance before the competition comparison. The viewer needs the scale of TSMC's lead before the yield and alternatives discussion.
scenes.information_role: TSMC controls ~90%+ of advanced-node manufacturing — not a modest lead, a near-monopoly.

required_assets.description: Supply chain diagram (sc09 state) + 90%+ stat card overlay: amber border, '90%+' large, '(analyst est.)' qualifier, fade sequence

scenes.description: Yield comparison — directional bar chart. Near-black background. Three horizontal bars, left-aligned, each labeled: (1) TSMC: amber fill, long bar, label 'Industry-leading yield (~65–70% est.)' in bone; (2) Samsung: graphite fill (#2A3142), medium-length bar, label 'Improving — ~50–60% late 2025' in muted steel; (3) Intel: muted steel fill, medium-short bar, label 'Internal use only' in muted steel — asterisk with footnote: 'Not available to fabless customers'. Title above: '2nm Node Yield — Directional Comparison' in IBM Plex Mono. GSAP: bars draw left to right in sequence (TSMC first, then Samsung, then Intel), each taking 0.6s. After all three drawn, Samsung bar animates: a ghost bar at 30% (early 2025) is shown briefly, then grows to 55–60% range — indicating the trajectory. This motion beat makes the improvement legible.
scenes.overlay_notes: Qualitative framing only per source_map c04/c05/c06 — no hard yield percentages as primary display numbers. Range estimates appear in bar labels, not as primary chart values. Intel bar must carry 'Internal use only' label prominently. Samsung trajectory animation is the key motion beat — makes the 'improving but trailing' point visual.
scenes.shot_intent: Show the yield gap as directional and structural — not a single moment in time. The Samsung trajectory prevents the comparison from being unfair to Samsung while still making the TSMC lead clear.
scenes.information_role: TSMC leads on yield. Samsung is improving but still behind. Intel is not a competitive alternative for fabless customers. The gap is real and consequential.

required_assets.description: GSAP directional bar chart: 3 bars with labeled ranges. Samsung trajectory animation (ghost bar grow). Intel 'internal only' footnote. Amber/graphite/steel fills.

scenes.description: Revenue stat card — primary source, hard number. Amber border, large '$35.90B' in Inter, sub-label '+40.6% YoY (USD)' in IBM Plex Mono, muted steel. Below: second line 'Q1 2026 — New Quarterly Record'. Appears at revenue narration beat. Holds 8s. Simultaneously: background of supply chain diagram returns at 15% opacity, Foundry node in amber — revenue card floats over the diagram context. On 'The chokepoint is not weakening' — revenue card fades out, diagram background comes to full opacity briefly, then sc15 cuts in.
scenes.overlay_notes: This is a primary-source hard stat — no qualifier needed. Hard number treatment appropriate. NVIDIA/Apple displacement is narration-only per source_map c10 guidance — no stat card for it.
scenes.shot_intent: Land the financial scale of the chokepoint. The revenue record makes the argument concrete: TSMC's dominance is not theoretical — it is reflected in its financial results.
scenes.information_role: TSMC's Q1 2026 revenue is a record. The chokepoint is strengthening under AI demand pressure.

scenes.description: Government investment — three-column stat card layout. Near-black background. GSAP: columns appear left to right with 0.5s stagger. Column 1: '$52B' (large, bone) / 'US CHIPS Act' (IBM Plex Mono, muted steel). Column 2: '€43B' (large, bone) / 'EU Chips Act'. Column 3: '¥3.9T' (large, bone) / 'Japan Subsidies'. Cyan (#3F8FA3) column header labels. Below all three: 'Every major government has assessed this as a strategic liability.' — bone, italic, Inter, smaller. Columns hold. After 20s, world map outline fades in at very low opacity behind the stat card — three point sources glow (US, EU, Japan) in muted steel. TSMC location in Taiwan glows amber. Visual: all investment paths point toward one amber node.
scenes.overlay_notes: ¥3.9T shown as yen figure — no USD conversion — per source_map c12 guidance. US ($52B) and EU (€43B) are primary-source public law, hard numbers appropriate. World map motif at low opacity — structural context, not focal element.
scenes.shot_intent: Show that the chokepoint is universally recognized. Three major economic blocs are all spending to address the same dependency — this signals the problem is real and large.
scenes.information_role: Every major government is trying to address TSMC dependency. The scale of investment signals the scale of the perceived risk.

required_assets.description: Three-column stat card (US/EU/Japan investment) + low-opacity world map with amber TSMC node and three muted glow points

scenes.description: Arizona node-generation framing. Near-black background. TSMC fab exterior hero visual (SVG/CSS) fades in, left-heavy composition. Node-generation stat card overlays on right: three stacked lines appear sequentially via GSAP stagger at 0.6s intervals — 'Arizona: N4 Now' (bone) / 'N3: est. 2027' (muted steel) / 'N2: No date set' (muted steel, dimmer). Deep system red border (#D64545) on stat card — inadequacy frame. After all three lines appear, a small arrow motif draws below: 'Two generations behind Taiwan's leading edge' — IBM Plex Mono, muted steel. Image holds. No amber in this scene — the Arizona story is a gap, not a leverage point.
scenes.overlay_notes: Red border on stat card signals inadequacy/gap per Asymmetric color rules — red only when showing cost, failure, or exposure. Do not use amber here. Three stagger states + arrow motif = 4 state changes across 20s.
scenes.shot_intent: Show that the Arizona investment, though real, addresses a different generation of technology. The red border is the only use of red in the video — it marks exactly where the exposure lives.
scenes.information_role: Arizona is producing N4 — two generations behind TSMC's leading edge. N3 not until 2027. N2 has no date. The investment is real; the gap is also real.

required_assets.description: SVG/CSS/GSAP Arizona fab scene — industrial building silhouette (graphite, amber face highlight), desert grid context, construction crane, node-generation stat card with red border: 3 GSAP stagger lines (N4 Now / N3 est. 2027 / N2 no date), arrow motif caption. Source: svg_native substitute for deferred ComfyUI image.

After 4s, text fades to 40% opacity as narration continues through the ecosystem explanation.
scenes.overlay_notes: Graphite background (not deep slate or near-black) distinguishes this scene visually as a quote moment. No amber — correct per brand rules. The quote holds while narration runs the ecosystem explanation; the text fades gracefully rather than cutting abruptly.
scenes.shot_intent: The founder of TSMC is the most credible possible source for the irreplaceability argument. His words land harder than any analyst claim. Let the quote hold space.
scenes.information_role: The man who built the system says it cannot be replicated. This is the strongest claim in the video and it comes from a primary source.

scenes.description: Leverage concept. Supply chain diagram returns (same state as end of sc09 — Foundry node amber, others dim). Narration: 'TSMC holds pricing power, schedule power, and strategic weight...' GSAP: three label tags animate into orbit around the amber Foundry node — 'Pricing Power', 'Schedule Power', 'Strategic Weight' — each tag a small amber-bordered pill, bone IBM Plex Mono text. Tags appear sequentially at 2s intervals. Tags hold. Then narration: 'Inside the primary chokepoint, there is a second one.' — all three tags retract, Foundry node pulses twice. Pause beat 1.5s. Then sc21 cuts in hard.
scenes.overlay_notes: Three label tags = three state changes (53s / 3 = ~17s each — compliant). The retraction and pulse before sc21 creates the pause beat for 'there is a second one' — critical for narration timing.
scenes.shot_intent: Name the three dimensions of leverage before introducing the nested chokepoint. The viewer needs to understand what 'leverage' means structurally before it's shown to be doubled.
scenes.information_role: TSMC's leverage is structural: pricing, schedule, strategic weight — not aggressive extraction. This sets up the CoWoS reveal as a second, separate leverage layer.

required_assets.description: Supply chain diagram (sc09 state) + GSAP: three amber-bordered label pills orbit Foundry node sequentially, then retract on 'second one' beat, node pulses twice

scenes.description: CoWoS second chokepoint reveal — second hero moment. Supply chain diagram persists. GSAP: (1) Foundry node expands vertically, splitting into two sub-layers — upper 'Wafer Fabrication' (cyan outline, smaller) and lower 'CoWoS Packaging' (amber outline, larger — it gets the signal color), (2) second amber border ring draws around the CoWoS sub-layer, (3) label appears: 'CoWoS — Advanced Packaging' in amber IBM Plex Mono, (4) a dependency arrow from CoWoS sub-layer connects outward to a new node labeled 'AI Accelerators (HBM)' in bone — indicating what this packaging enables, (5) amber glow on CoWoS sub-layer pulses once and stabilizes. Visual: chokepoint inside a chokepoint. Two amber borders visible simultaneously.
scenes.overlay_notes: This is the second hero moment — the nested chokepoint is the most analytically surprising claim in the video. The dual amber border is intentional — two control layers visible at once. This is the only time two amber elements share the frame.
scenes.shot_intent: Make the nested structure visual. The viewer must see that there is a chokepoint inside the chokepoint — this is not a metaphor, it is a separate process layer.
scenes.information_role: CoWoS is a separate process from wafer fabrication. It is also controlled by TSMC. It is also sold out. The dependency doubles.

required_assets.description: GSAP: Foundry node splits into Wafer Fab (cyan) and CoWoS Packaging (amber) sub-layers. Second amber ring draws. AI Accelerator dependency arrow. Dual amber glow stable.

scenes.description: CoWoS capacity stat card + growth bar. Near-black background. Stat card: '~130K wpm' (large, bone, Inter) with amber border and label 'Projected CoWoS capacity end-2026 / Still sold out' (IBM Plex Mono, muted steel). Below stat card: a horizontal capacity growth bar — two labeled positions: '35K wpm (2024)' on left (graphite fill), '~130K wpm (late 2026)' on right (amber fill). Bar fills left to right via GSAP over 1.5s. Sub-label: 'Near-fourfold increase / Still insufficient to meet demand' — bone, smaller. Appears after bar fill completes.
scenes.overlay_notes: Tilde (~) on stat card value signals projection per source_map c08 guidance. 'Still sold out' label sourced from c09 (high confidence). Growth bar is a visual argument: even a 4x increase is insufficient.
scenes.shot_intent: Quantify the capacity crunch. The 4x growth number sounds large; the 'still sold out' label immediately undercuts it. Both facts together make the argument.
scenes.information_role: CoWoS capacity is growing fast but demand is growing faster. Fully booked through 2026. This is not a temporary supply chain disruption.

required_assets.description: CoWoS stat card (~130K wpm) + GSAP capacity growth bar (35K→~130K, graphite to amber fill, 1.5s draw) + 'still insufficient' sub-label

scenes.description: Abstract convergence diagram — third hero moment. Near-black background. Five abstract source nodes appear as bone-labeled tiles: 'Apple', 'NVIDIA', 'AMD', 'Qualcomm', and 'AI Data Centers'. Each source node emits a cyan route line (GSAP draw) that curves toward a single central chokepoint node. The chokepoint node is a stacked card labeled 'TSMC / Taiwan' (IBM Plex Mono label line), and it alone is amber (#F5A400). As each route arrives, the amber node pulses brighter and slightly larger; the source node dims. Final state: all cyan routes locked into the amber TSMC node, with a small sub-label appearing last: 'No volume alternative'.
scenes.overlay_notes: No geography. Interface-driven leverage map. State changes: (1) nodes appear staggered, (2) each cyan route draws in sequence (5 arrivals), (3) amber chokepoint pulses on each arrival, (4) final sub-label appears. Color semantics: cyan = structure/flows; amber = chokepoint/control only.
scenes.shot_intent: Make the geopolitical dependency physical. All of global AI hardware demand converges on one point on a map. This is the visual argument for the entire video.
scenes.information_role: Everything — AI, cloud, phones, defense — converges on one geographic location. Both the wafer fabrication and the packaging process are there. One company controls both.

scenes.description: Full leverage map — dependency tree. Supply chain diagram (Foundry node amber) returns. GSAP: from the TSMC node, a dependency tree branches downward with four labeled leaf nodes: 'AI Training Clusters' / 'Consumer Devices' / 'Cloud Infrastructure' / 'Defense Systems'. Each leaf appears with a stagger of 0.8s. Leaf nodes: bone text, muted steel borders — they are dependent, not controlling. All four leaves are connected to TSMC with cyan arrows (dependency flow). As narration delivers 'the leverage map looks like this' — TSMC node flares amber, all four dependency nodes pulse once and stabilize. Then each of three key facts appears as a small IBM Plex Mono label on the amber node: '90%+ share (analyst est.)' → 'No viable substitute' → 'Timeline: years, not months'. Each replaces the previous with a cut (not fade).
scenes.overlay_notes: Three label replacements on TSMC node = 3 state changes. Four leaf stagger = 4 more. Total 7+ state changes across 78s. Labels use analyst-est. qualifier on 90% per source_map c03. This is the synthesis diagram — every previous visual motif is present.
scenes.shot_intent: Show the full leverage map in one frame. The viewer has seen each piece separately — this scene assembles them. Everything depends on TSMC; TSMC has no substitute.
scenes.information_role: The leverage map is complete: one node, four dependent domains, no substitutes, long timeline. The viewer can now answer 'where is the leverage?' in one diagram.

required_assets.description: Supply chain + dependency tree: 4 leaf nodes (AI/devices/cloud/defense), TSMC amber flare, three cycling IBM Plex Mono label replacements on TSMC node

scenes.description: Final stat card — three-line summary. Amber border, deep slate background. GSAP stagger lines appear one at a time at 1s intervals: (1) '90%+ advanced-node share (analyst est.)' — bone, Inter; (2) 'Arizona: N4 now — N3 est. 2027' — muted steel, smaller; (3) 'Structural dependency: unchanged until 2028+' — muted steel, smaller. Full card holds through end of narration section. No motion after third line appears — static hold is intentional for emphasis.
scenes.overlay_notes: Three stagger state changes. Static hold at end is correct — this is the conclusion, not a build. First and only time in the video that a static hold >4s is intentional: the final summary deserves uninterrupted reading time.
scenes.shot_intent: Leave the viewer with the three key facts in one frame. This is the takeaway card — designed for screenshot and sharing.
scenes.information_role: Three facts to leave with: market share, Arizona gap, dependency timeline. All hedged correctly per source_map.

required_assets.description: Three-line stat card: amber border, stagger reveal at 1s intervals, static hold. Lines: 90%+ (analyst est.) / AZ: N4 now, N3 est. 2027 / Dependency until 2028+

transition_rules.between_diagram_builds: cut — state changes within GSAP timeline, not scene-level transitions

animatic_rules.red_usage: sc17 only — Arizona node-generation stat card border. One instance total.
animatic_rules.cyan_usage: Supply chain arrows and non-focal nodes. Structural layer only.

animatic_rules.no_logos: Company wordmarks only (bone text in boxes). No brand logo assets needed.
animatic_rules.static_hold_exception: sc26 final stat card is permitted to hold static after the third line appears — intentional conclusion beat

hold_rules.stat_cards: 8s primary, fade to 30% opacity rather than disappear where background context is useful
hold_rules.pull_quote: 4s full opacity, then fade to 40% while narration continues
hold_rules.final_stat_card: Static hold from 3rd line appearance to end of sc26 — intentional exception to 4s rule
